data.title: Bessent Leaves Door Open to Jensen Huang's Return to Nvidia
data.description: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent no longer ruled out Jensen Huang’s return to Nvidia, eight days after demanding an outside CEO, as the stock traded about 48% below its 52-week high. Shares fell 14% Friday to close at $125.53, then rose to $130.01 after hours, according to BeInCrypto. Huang resigned Nov. 12 after reports of extramarital affairs, including one involving a woman U.S. officials suspect of ties to Chinese intelligence. Three days later, Bessent called for a dramatic shake-up and gave Nvidia’s board and lawyers 10 days to answer export-compliance questions. On Sunday, responding to CBS host Margaret Brennan about President Donald Trump’s call for Huang’s reinstatement, Bessent said officials needed to see where responsibility lay; Trump had said two days earlier that Huang should apologize and return. Board chair Harvey Jones said Nov. 17 that the board did not intend to reinstate Huang, hours after Huang said he would return if allowed. Bessent said Treasury still needs answers and wants to know whether Megaspeed was a pass-through company. Nvidia also faces a reported SEC accounting inquiry. Options imply an 11.5% move in either direction by the Nov. 27 expiry, with an estimated range of roughly $115 to $145. TipRanks’ 44 analysts have an average 12-month target of $232.59, about 85% above Friday’s close; 30 rate the stock Buy, 13 Hold and one Sell. The lowest target is $130.

data.title: China, Korea and Taiwan Prepare Stock Rescues Ahead of Monday as S&P 500 Extends Losses
data.description:
China, Korea and Taiwan moved to support their stock markets ahead of Monday as the S&P 500 entered the session on a seven-day losing streak, its longest since February 2020. South Korea prepared a $7.3 billion stabilization fund, China will lower minimum margin requirements to 80% from 100% starting November 30, and Taiwan restricted short selling below the previous day’s close, according to BeInCrypto. South Korea’s finance minister called an emergency meeting with the central bank chief and three regulators on Sunday to try to prevent a “Black Monday.” China’s changes are expected to free up 400 billion yuan for stock purchases. Taiwan’s state fund has been buying shares since November 6, but the market still recorded its worst week since 1991.

The moves matter to Wall Street because Asian and U.S. markets are linked by the AI chip trade. Nvidia fell 14% on Friday, while AMD’s five-day decline exceeded 24%. Trend-following computer-driven funds sold $57 billion in stocks over a month; Goldman Sachs models project another $28.6 billion in sales if prices rise and $80.6 billion if they fall. JPMorgan Asset Management’s David Kelly called the selloff “not a fatal illness,” noting that the S&P 500 rose in the three months after 17 of 22 corrections since 1980, although five of 14 similar declines since 1983 became bear markets. Goldman said a softer Federal Reserve could mark a bottom, while traders priced a 91.4% chance of a December rate hike. U.S. futures reopen at 6 p.m. ET on Sunday, with Seoul markets opening an hour later.

data.title: Fusionist Attack-Related Minting, Tornado and Cross-Chain Bridge Addresses Disclosed
data.description: Addresses linked to the Fusionist attack, including the attacker’s minting address, a Tornado router contract and the exploited cross-chain bridge, have been disclosed. According to Odaily, Onchain Lens identified the attacker’s minting address and a third address as 0x1029...e12c5, the second wallet as 0xb335...019b5, the Tornado router contract as 0xB6f0...01703, its sender as 0xFF85...0CFB, and the exploited bridge contract as 0x9d06...5915.

data.title: STOCKS | Goldman Traders See US Selloff as Buying Opportunity, Warn of Positioning Risks
